title: Vintage Shopping in Berlin - Quick Summary
items: **Berlin is still one of Europe's best second-hand cities, but the bargains are smaller than the reputation.** The scene has shifted toward curated, higher-priced shops. Come for the hunt and the quality, not for cheap.

**Pick one district and work it on foot instead of crossing the whole city.** Neukolln around Weserstrasse has the densest run of small curated shops. Friedrichshain around Boxhagener Platz is the budget end. Kreuzberg on Bergmannstrasse is where you go for the pay-by-weight kilo store. Mitte is designer resale and the most central. Prenzlauer Berg is polished, with Mauerpark next door.

**Kilo shops charge by weight, not by piece.** At Colours on Bergmannstrasse and Made in Berlin in Mitte, clothes are grouped by coloured tags and weighed at the till, so light shirts and dresses are the real value and a heavy coat can eat your budget.

**Nearly every vintage shop is shut on Sunday.** Berlin's shop-closing law keeps them closed, so plan your vintage day for Monday to Saturday. On a Sunday the flea markets, Mauerpark and Boxhagener Platz above all, are the second-hand option instead.
**Carry some cash.** The big chains take cards, but the small owner-run shops in Neukolln and Kreuzberg often prefer it, and a few set card minimums.

**My free walking tour ends at Hackescher Markt, a two-minute walk from the Mitte vintage streets.** Do the walk in the morning to get your bearings, then browse Mulackstrasse and Neue Schonhauser Strasse in the afternoon.
